newsitem.title: USA: Mexico Brady debt mixed on drug-war certification.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Brady debt mixed on drug-war certification.

text.p: The "certification" of Mexico as a U.S. partner in the war on drugs, which had been widely anticipated, was greeted with relief in the emerging debt market, traders and analysts said.
"We have expected a full certification for Mexico," said Omar Borla, chief Latin America economist at Robert Fleming, Inc.
Mexico Bradies improved marginally from early decline after comments from Washington officials indicated that Mexico would be certified. The official announcement was made at 1630 EST/2130 GMT.
The cerfication, neverthelelss, was a relief after uncertainties mounted in recent weeks amid scandals involving Mexico's top anti-drug army general and other officials, traders said.
A "decertification" would cut Mexico off most forms of economic assistance and loans from international institutions. Colombia was decertified for the second year in a row.
Mexico Pars MX625L19=RR edged up 1/4 to 76-1/8 bid and Discount MXFLL19=RR was unchanged at 91-3/8 bid.
The performance of Mexico Bradies was unremarkable in the market that calmed down somewhat after two days of heavy selling, traders said.
After opening on a downbeat, Brady prices began recovering in late morning on short-covering, but jitters remained, they said.
"People are nervous about the Treasuries," said a trader with an investment bank. "Next week would be crucial."
Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan on Wednesday jolted the market during his testimony to the Congress in which he singled out inflated asset prices as a cause for concern.

The worries about a pre-emptive monetary tightening nearly overshadowed all other developments in the market. "We may have reached a high-water mark on spread narrowing on our market for a while," said a fund manager gloomily.
Some traders noted that, in addition to hedge funds, "crossover" investors from insurance companies also joined the fray, but others said the liquidation was not signficant.
Argentina fared the best when Brady pricies crawled out of the lows, traders said.
Argentina Discounts AR425C23=RR managed to add 1/2 to bid 83.00 even. Argentina FRBs ARFLC05=RR was bid 90-1/4, down 1/4 on the day.
By contrast, Brazil C BR8D14=RR remained out of favor at 79.00 bid, off 7/8.
Ecuador failed to excite the market with its upcoming announcement of President Fabian Alarcon's "economic plan."
"It's going to be cosmetic," said Fleming's Borla.
As the head of a a care-taker government before a presidential election is called, Alarcon is unlikely to launch ambitious economic reform that drove President Abdala Bucaram out of office, he said.
Carlos Janada, analyst at Morgan Stanley, agreed that Alarcon's weak position in the coalition government precludes any meaningful reform.
"There's no incentive for Alarcon to take tough measures," he said.
